warning_classification.finding: Installed Starlette warns that its httpx TestClient support is deprecated. This is a dependency maintenance warning from test transport import, not evidence that the production browser or API worker crashed.
warning_classification.evidence: The exact warning is retained in full-suite stdout; FastAPI/Starlette source files and package versions are hash-bound below.
warning_classification.action_taken: None; dependencies and locked environment were left unchanged.

warning_classification.finding: The negative test intentionally appends a duplicate wheel member, then requires the wheel verifier to reject it with BSK_WHEEL_MISSING_OR_DUPLICATE_METADATA. Its XML testcase passed. The warning does not show that an installed production wheel was corrupted.
warning_classification.evidence: The test source and CPython zipfile warning location are identified by the original warning summary; the test's passed XML record is retained.
warning_classification.action_taken: None; the warning and original test result remain intact.

warning_classification.finding: The installed Win32 probe first runs powershell.exe with Get-CimInstance, then attempts WMIC when the first path fails. PowerShell exists; Get-CimInstance reports PermissionDenied/HRESULT 0x80041003 in this environment. The WMIC executable is missing. The outer helper catches the failure, caches 'not found', warns, and returns the available logical-core count.
warning_classification.action_taken: No WMIC installation, permission elevation, LOKY_MAX_CPU_COUNT setting or warning suppression was performed.

warning_classification.finding: This is a real unhandled text-decoding exception in a child-command stderr reader. The hidden UTF8 minimal probe reproduces the historical signature exactly: invalid UTF8 byte 0xbe at position 18. The failing raw byte payload decodes as the PowerShell Get-CimInstance permission-denied message under CP936. WMIC fails at process creation and does not account for that reader payload.
warning_classification.exact_original_and_reproduced_signature: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xbe in position 18: invalid start byte
warning_classification.attribution: Third-party physical-core detection subprocess text pipe, not a Basilisk integration worker, simulation state owner, HTTP request handler, frontend event loop or WebSocket reader.
warning_classification.qualification: The original full-suite traceback does not include the subprocess owner arguments. Attribution is supported by matching installed call sites plus an isolated reproduction with the same hidden/UTF8 conditions and raw PowerShell diagnostic payload. The reproduction's thread target/owner introspection fields were already cleared by CPython and remain null in the raw evidence; no missing owner metadata was invented.
warning_classification.action_taken: Original exception hook and warning output retained; no filter, error-tolerant decoder or dependency patch was applied.

installed_call_chain.fact: The scientific-closure test fits LogisticRegression, RandomForestClassifier(n_jobs=-1), and HistGradientBoostingClassifier analysis baselines.
The installed gradient-boosting fit path obtains effective OpenMP threads through _openmp_effective_n_threads().
The default only_physical_cores=True path calls joblib.cpu_count when no overriding OpenMP thread setting is used.
joblib.cpu_count delegates to loky.cpu_count with the same only_physical_cores option.
Win32 probe invokes PowerShell Get-CimInstance with capture_output=True,text=True and no explicit encoding; bare except then falls back to WMIC.
Probe errors become cached 'not found'; cpu_count warns on the first failure and returns aggregate logical availability.
With UTF8 mode, implicit text decoding uses UTF8. On Windows, stdout/stderr are TextIOWrapper pipes read by _readerthread helper threads.

The historical full-suite driver explicitly sets PYTHONUTF8=1 for its children and uses CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows. The diagnostic uses interpreter -X utf8 to select the same decoder without changing environment variables.
